# Glass, gradients and liquid materials

Visual polish requires optics and restraint.

**Glass:** start with a CSS fallback, only add one WebGL glass effect if it improves affordances. Confirm WebGL2 support, compositing cost, touch behaviour, readable contrast, and fallback on reduced motion.

**Liquid metal:** build original shaders or use rendered assets generated by permitted tools. Liquid Logo is an app and visual reference, not necessarily a component dependency. Treat shaders and exported graphics independently for licensing.

**Gradients:** ShaderGradient README says MIT, but no recognised root GitHub licence. Recheck package-specific terms, attribution and embedded asset rights. CSS gradients/Canvas2D can often replace GPU effects more efficiently.

**Licensing:** Do not vendor Lygia without reviewing its Prosperity/Patron licence. Do not redistribute React Bits source as a competing components pack. Do not copy Zeroxy source without an explicit licence. Archived Lamina is not a recommended new dependency.

**Design rule:** a polished interface should use limited well-directed effects, not glass on every object.
